title: Dead Zones Enable Flexible Phase Organization in Coupled Oscillators
summary: Coupled oscillator networks underlie many biological systems, from cardiac cycles to circadian rhythms. Phase-reduced models such as the Kuramoto model have been widely used to study synchronization, but they typically assume that oscillators remain continuously responsive to inputs and often produce tightly clustered phase distributions. Biological oscillators, however, commonly exhibit phase intervals during which inputs have little or no effect, called ``dead zones."
